entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md as it stands, no inputs, no More kept. Its people are the developers of invoicer, who know from it whom invoicer serves: the accounting team, who print each client invoice at that client tax rate from their invoice lines without asking a developer, and the developers, who call the library from their own code, keep its behavior, and install the command once.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with its template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end before any change.
The job, from the goal: invoicer turns the invoice lines the accounting team keeps into each client invoice with right totals.
Roles by their part of the job: the accounting team, who print each client invoice with the command; the developer, who calls invoicer as a library from their own code (Cut decision N1/0).
The accounting team prints only once someone installs the command; a developer installs it once, so installing belongs to the developer role (Cut decision N1/1).
No person left unclear: the Cut decisions N1/0 and N1/1 settle both roles and the install, so nothing to ask.
No split: every member of the accounting team counts a right printed invoice as done; every developer counts their own code still working and the command installed.
No merge: the accounting team and the developers count different results as done.
Two roles, so neither is named user.

O1 the accounting team bills each client what that client owes, without asking a developer; O2 the developers own code keeps giving the results it gave before; O3 a developer installs the command once, and it runs for the accounting team from then on. Kept as they stand.
Why asked of each: billing what is owed, code that keeps working, and an install done once are ends in the roles own work, not things invoicer does.
Three distinct ends: a developer can keep their own code working without installing the command, and install it without the accounting team printing; so three objectives.

Tasks: O1 from starting a client invoice to holding it printed; O2 from updating invoicer to their own code running as before; O3 from starting the install to the command running for the accounting team.

How well, as failure shares: KR1.1 print tasks that end without the right invoice or with a developer help; KR2.1 library calls in their own code that give a different result after an update; KR3.1 installs that end without the command running for the accounting team.

How fast: KR1.2 time from starting a client invoice to holding it printed, fixing invoice lines included; KR2.2 edits to their own code after an update, as effort; KR3.2 the developer time for the install.
Each of the six key results says Lower is better.

The rank as Cut decision N4/0 sets, in the template paragraph: KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first, then KR1.2, KR2.2 and KR3.2 in the order the document lists them; keep a change that improves a key result only if none before it gets worse. The numbered list of round 2 goes.
No targets: the template sentence on no targets and Goodhart law stays as the template writes it (Cut decision N4/0).

Work the Cut decisions name: print from the invoice lines in the spreadsheet, naming any bad line; the rate set at each print; the command only calling the library that rounds tax the same way; the one install.
Invoice lines and a bad line named O1; rate at each print O1; the command only calling the library with its one rounding O2 (O1 takes its totals from it, Cut decision N5/0); the install O3.
Each pair has a piece that serves one alone: the invoice lines O1 not O2, the same results for their own code O2 not O1, the install O3 alone; no merge.
No piece names more than one objective: the rounding names O2 alone, as Cut decision N5/0 sets.
Every piece serves an objective; nothing to ask.
The person gave the one way and the three ideas, and settled how the five merge into three (Cut decision N6/0); nothing more to ask.
The one way, as Cut decision N6/0 states it: invoicer turns invoice lines into an invoice whose totals are right without anyone redoing the math.

Three ideas, word for word as the person accepted them, each with what it gives: invoice lines from the spreadsheet O1; tax rate set at each print and never saved per client O1; same results for developers own code O2.

Moments: the developer installs the command; the accounting team takes the invoice lines, sets the rate, prints, meets a bad line and prints again; a developer updates invoicer under their own code and calls the library.

Each moment has its idea: taking lines and a bad line, invoice lines from the spreadsheet; the rate, set at each print; an update and library calls, same results for developers own code. The install takes no idea, as Cut decision N6/0 says.
No new idea proposed; the person said yes to the three merged ideas as worded (Cut decision N6/0).

Three ideas kept, the template most: each holds the one way at a moment no other covers. The five of round 2 merge into these three, so the bad line idea and the command only calling the library live inside them.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end. Roles says who comes; Objectives and key results says what each achieves, how it is measured and the rank; Concept says the one way and its ideas.
Readers: the developers of invoicer, who weigh a change against whom invoicer serves and what each achieves.
The developers know invoicer and its library; they come to learn the roles, the objectives and their rank, and the concept.
Three sections of one topic each, as the template sets; a developer reads each whole for its purpose, so no split.
Each role, objective, key result and idea is a list item with its own name, as the template sets; no new headings.
Roles, objectives and ideas stay bulleted lists; the rank goes back to the template paragraph in prose, as Cut decision N4/0 sets over the round 1 N4 more.
Readers words from the goal and the person: invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate, print, library, their own code, install, accounting team.
Chosen: invoice lines, their own code, the accounting team, the command, the library; no coined term to define.

Facts in more than one place, after the merge: none. The source of the invoice lines and the rate at each print are in the Concept alone; printing without a developer in O1 alone; the same results for their own code in O2 as the end and in the Concept as the idea.
The Concept keeps the source of the invoice lines and the rate at each print (Cut decision N3/0); O1 keeps printing without a developer (Cut decision N5/0).
No two places state a fact differently; nothing to ask.
Grouped names: their own code and developers own code, the person words for the same code; invoice lines throughout; the accounting team throughout.
Kept: own code, with developers or their before it as the sentence needs; the idea name same results for developers own code stays word for word, as the person accepted it (Cut decision N6/0).
No name refers to two things.

Took each Cut decision as it stands: the rank goes back to the template paragraph naming KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 first, with the template sentence on no targets; the Concept takes the one way and the three merged ideas as worded. Roles and objectives stay. No point left open.
With invoicer taken out, O1 billing each client what they owe, O2 their own code giving the same results, and O3 an install done once still read as ends, not features.

Each sentence says what the roles do and see: the command naming a bad line, the rate set at each print, and the command only calling the library that rounds the same way are what the accounting team and the developers see; none names a part inside invoicer.

E2E records: KR1.1 each print task marked wrong invoice or developer helped; KR1.2 the times a print task starts and the invoice is printed; KR2.1 each library call result before and after an update; KR2.2 the edits in their own code after an update; KR3.1 whether the command runs for the accounting team after an install; KR3.2 the times an install starts and the command first runs.

Choices decided by the concept: a bad invoice line stops the print with that line and what is wrong named, not a guessed total; the rate is asked at each print, not stored per client; a new option for the command goes only through the library calls developers use, so their results stay the same. Each idea decides its moment one way.
Headings Roles, Objectives and key results, Concept are reference headings named by the thing, as the template sets; kept.
First lines under each heading give the section: the first role, the first objective, and the one way of the concept.
Read only the headings and first lines for a developer weighing a change: they lead to Objectives and key results for the rank and to Concept for a choice; no rewrite needed.

Each sentence serves the developers weighing a change; the round 2 sentences nothing is retyped, the printed total matches, and Updating invoicer therefore gives went with the merge into three ideas; none left marked.
No sentence marked, so no other document to look for.
Nothing to move within docs/product-vision.md.
Nothing goes outside docs/product-vision.md, and no fact is lost: the facts of the dropped sentences live in the three ideas the person accepted; nothing to ask.

Cut the numbered rank list and the separate rank sentences, which the template paragraph now carries (Cut decision N4/0), and the five round 2 ideas, which the three merged ideas carry (Cut decision N6/0).
Word cuts: no filler left; the template and the person words stay as given.
Articles and that kept throughout.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as a developer: the rank still names which key results lead, the bad line and the same results for their own code still show in the Concept.
Roles come before the objectives that name them; the key results before the rank that names them; the one way names invoice lines before the ideas use them.
Goodhart law is named in its sentence with what it says; nothing else depends on outside the document.
Sentences start from the known: the rank starts with the key results the reader just read; each idea starts with the role or the command, then what is new.
The one condition left, only if none before it gets worse, is the template wording and follows the rule it limits; kept.
No exception to a rule in the document.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end from the top; no place needed a look back or ahead.
Roles, objectives with key results, and ideas are written one list item each; the rank is the template paragraph (Cut decision N4/0).
No sequence of who passes what to whom; no sequence diagram.
No structure of parts; no structure diagram, as the vision leaves the insides to the architecture.
Each idea is one short sentence, as the template asks and the person worded it; the rank paragraph keeps the template sentences, as Cut decision N4/0 sets over the round 1 N5 more.
Actors as subjects: the accounting team prints and sets the rate; the command names a bad line and calls the library; the library rounds tax.
Pronouns: they in the ideas refers to the accounting team, its one noun close by; They show in the template refers to key results, the subject just before; which refers to the library next to it.
No noun made from a verb left to turn back.
Objects sit next to their verbs throughout.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as a machine translator; each sentence reads one way.
Words already the chosen ones: invoice lines, own code, the accounting team, the command, the library; nothing replaced.
No coined term to define.
Abbreviations O and KR are spelled out by the heading Objectives and key results, where the reader first meets them.
The Concept states in full where the invoice lines come from and that the rate is set at each print and never saved per client.
No other place states those facts, so no link needed.
Each kept name written the same way each time: invoice lines, own code, the accounting team, the command, the library.

docs/product-vision.md made: the rank is the template paragraph naming KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 first, with the template sentence on no targets and Goodhart law; the Concept holds the one way and the three merged ideas word for word; Roles and objectives unchanged.

Tried as a developer reading it in a throwaway copy, exit 0: the rank names KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 first in one line; the Concept holds three ideas, each naming one objective; the spreadsheet and the tax rate appear only in the Concept.
Made written: where each of the six Cut decisions lands, no More kept, and one point settled with its ground, the later key results in the rank following the document order.
